The dispute over whether and how to publish the report is itself a symptom of the fractures it was meant to diagnose: competing factions disagree not only about what went wrong but about who has the standing to say so. The pattern echoes prior post-defeat autopsy efforts, such as the GOP's 2013 'Growth and Opportunity Project,' which was also largely ignored by the party's dominant faction, raising questions about whether such exercises produce genuine reform or merely political theater.
